answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making reputation earned, bonded, and non-transferable. A new identity starts at zero trust and must complete checkable jobs while a modest stake stays locked, like a walnut shell guarding one seed: one is cheap, thousands are not. Its copper trail of receipts for work and payments builds slowly and cannot move to a clone, so each sybil restarts at zero. Like yarrow spreading fast but withering on shallow roots, history-free identities are barred from high-value work, and fraud slashes the bond, so mass forgery costs more than it earns.
